relay.text: RdeA transfers phosphate to RegA Asp212 (His-Asp phospho-relay, both directions)

rega_20.text: phosphorylation activates RegA phosphodiesterase at least 20-fold

rega_km.text: RegA cAMP phosphodiesterase domain: Km about 5 uM

rega_loss.text: inhibition of the PDE (loss of RegA) increases PKA activity and affects terminal differentiation

circuit.text: cAMP activates PKA, PKA inhibits ERK2 and loses ERK2 control, ERK2 phosphorylates RegA and lowers cAMP (Laub and Loomis circuit)

erk_phase.text: ERK2 activation oscillates in phase with cAMP peaks

pka_erk.text: PKA regulates ERK2 activation and adaptation (pka- cells: lower, more extended activation)

erk_rega.text: ERK2 modulates cAMP levels through RegA; ERK2 may phosphorylate and inhibit RegA

bader2007.start: Intracellular cAMP is degraded by the DdPDE2, a class I enzyme regulated by histidine kinase/phospho-relay

thomason1999.start: Phosphorylation of RegA by a heterologous phospho-donor protein activates RegA phosphodiesterase activity at least 20-fold
Phospho-transfer is dependent on the presumed phospho-accepting amino acids, histidine 65 of RdeA and aspartate 212 of RegA, and occurs in both directions

thomason1998.start: One domain is a cAMP phosphodiesterase (Km ~5 μM)
It can accept phosphate from acetyl phosphate in a reaction typical of RRs, with transfer dependent on Asp212

shaulsky1998.start: Genetic analyses indicate that inhibition of the phosphodiesterase results in an increase in the activity of PKA, which acts at a check point for terminal differentiation

aubry1997.start: In this study we show that other pathways required for aggregation, including Ras and cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA), are important regulators of ERK2 activation and adaptation
PKA overexpression results in a more rapid, higher level of activation, whereas pka null cells show a lower level but more extended ERK2 activation

laub1998.start: A rise in the internal concentration of cAMP activates protein kinase A such that it inhibits ERK2

maeda2004.start: We have observed spontaneous oscillations in activation of the mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinase ERK2 that occur in phase with peaks of cAMP
we show that ERK2 modulates cAMP levels through the phosphodiesterase RegA
ERK2 may directly inhibit phosphodiesterase activity by phosphorylation of RegA
Cells lacking PKA return more slowly to basal ERK2 activity, whereas constitutive PKA activity leads to greatly reduced ERK2 activity after stimulation with cAMP
